_comment: Quiet changelog. Entries newest first. lastChecked = month of the most recent re-verification pass (prices/guidance); bump it on each check. kinds: item | price | recheck | gear | copy | guide

entries.text: Cornflakes may contain milk, nuts, peanuts and soya, so they are now left out when any of those allergies is ticked. Aldi's website doesn't show allergens, so for foods priced at Aldi we use the warnings from the label we checked, plus anything known about the Aldi product.

Checked the price of every food in the three-day basket on the Aldi website, or Sainsbury's where Aldi had no match. Shop prices may differ. Some pack sizes changed: oatcakes 250g, raisins 500g, dried mango 100g, honey 454g, tuna 145g. Where a shop's page didn't say how much of a tin is drained weight, we count the smaller amount and mark the price as an estimate. Sardine and salmon prices are still estimates.
Longer-store plans also leave out honey when a child under 4 is counted, and both planners now say why: honey isn't safe for babies under one.

Checked the allergens on the label of every food in the three-day basket. You can now tick allergies in your household, and the basket leaves out foods that contain them or may contain them. No honey when a child under 4 is counted, as honey isn't safe for babies under one. Dark chocolate is no longer counted as gluten-free, as its label says it isn't suitable for a wheat allergy. Added flapjack and cornflakes to the three-day basket.

Both planners now ask how many children are in each age group: under 4, 4 to 10, and 11 to 17. Each group gets its own calorie figure (1,000, 1,600 and 2,000 a day), instead of the same 1,200 for every child. Plans for older children are bigger; plans for toddlers are smaller. Added a link to the government advice the figures come from, and a reminder to keep a baby's usual milk or formula.

Added two gluten-free starchy foods you can eat cold: gluten-free oat crackers and gluten-free rice cakes, both labelled gluten free. Every three-day basket now includes a starchy food. The gluten-free ones only appear when the gluten-free filter is ticked, so other households still get ordinary oatcakes.

Checked the calories of every food in the three-day basket against a named product label. We had been counting the whole weight on the tin, including the water you pour away, so a tin of chickpeas was counted at more than double what you actually eat. Some dry foods were counted too low. Plans now count what you actually eat. Added a tin opener to the list, a note on opened tins when there's no fridge, and clearer wording on water for washing and cooking.
New front page and three-day planner, built around the government's Be Ready advice. Added a note on how we use AI. Fixed broken links and some display problems.
Stock cubes/bouillon corrected to £0.35 per 60g (Aldi own-brand, scaled). Tinned salmon and raisins marked as estimates — no Aldi/Lidl equivalent to verify against.
Added 'eat straight from the tin' badges and a small comfort line to every plan.
Guide pages re-verified, with check dates shown and a build-time check that keeps them current.
Tinned mackerel corrected to £0.85 per 125g tin, matching typical own-brand pricing.
Added gear suggestions: vacuum storage, water purification, foil blanket, fire blanket, extinguisher, water butt, shelving and under-bed boxes.
Added sprouting and microgreens guidance to the micronutrients section, and an important-documents note to the readiness check.
